tasks.title: Constrained mathematics
tasks.summary: One parametric optimization problem, six regimes, a complete proof and executable formulas.
tasks.question: Minimize x² + 2y² + 3z² + xy − yz + (2 − 2t)x + 5y + z, for every t ∈ [−2, 4].
tasks.feasibleSet: x + y + z = 1; x, y, z ≥ 0; x ≤ 3/5; 2y + z ≥ 1/2. The plot shows each submitted solver’s sampled objective value.

checks.label: Numerical optimizer and feasibility
checks.detail: 1233 of 1233 parameter probes passed for this one problem. This does not replace a proof.

checks.label: Global existence uniqueness
checks.detail: The feasible polygon is explicitly described with its five vertices and compactness. The positive quadratic form is correct for H=[[8,8],[8,12]] and proves strict convexity on the equality plane; the stated uniqueness conclusion follows.

checks.label: Complete piecewise optimizer
checks.detail: All six coordinate formulas and the five exact transitions match the independently derived reference. The closed intervals cover [-2,4]. The nonzero-length fixed vertex interval [-1/2,0] is explicitly present, not skipped.

checks.label: Exact value function
checks.detail: Every displayed value polynomial is algebraically identical to the exact reference, including C written as 4-(5+2t)^2/16. Values at transitions and domain endpoints are also correct. This assessment uses symbolic expressions, not numerical sample success.

checks.label: Primal feasibility
checks.detail: The complete coordinate table and explicit closed interval bounds make all five inequalities directly checkable. Independent algebraic inspection verifies sums of one, nonnegative coordinates, x<=3/5 and 2y+z>=1/2 in every row. The proof retains z>=0 in the polygon and correctly establishes its positive slack along the solution.

checks.label: Dual stationarity certificate
checks.detail: The original-variable Lagrangian and its sign convention are explicit. All five inequality multipliers, including the global gamma=0, and the equality multiplier are supplied for all six regimes. The three original stationarity equations and the reduction used to verify the table are correct.

checks.label: Dual feasibility complementarity
checks.detail: All listed multipliers are nonnegative on their stated closed intervals. Only tight constraints carry nonzero multipliers. The corner row has beta=-2t and epsilon=1+2t, which are simultaneously nonnegative precisely on [-1/2,0]. Boundary zero multipliers are explicitly distinguished from inactive constraints.

checks.label: Closed transition analysis
checks.detail: Each transition is derived from a multiplier sign change or newly binding constraint, and the full transition table correctly supplies optimizer, active constraints, zero/nonzero multipliers, value and derivative. The matching coordinate/value/multiplier formulas are correct. The six derivative formulas V'(t)=-2x(t) match from both sides, and the proof explicitly states C1 with one-sided domain-endpoint derivatives. Thus the amended mandatory continuity/differentiability requirement is met.

checks.label: Global all real sufficiency
checks.detail: The proof uses stationarity, affine constraints and complementarity to make the gradient term nonnegative for every feasible competitor. The exact positive quadratic remainder proves strict global superiority over every distinct point. Complete coverage by the six closed intervals proves the all-real-parameter assertion and excludes unexamined faces without relying on a numerical optimizer.

Fabius took longer and emitted more output tokens in both math pairs: 353.080 s / 16,631 tokens versus 298.763 s / 15,120 in the first; 288.597 s / 14,650 versus 262.152 s / 12,959 in the second. These shared-environment timings describe the runs, not an isolated speed benchmark.

lessons: All four landing pages pass the seven recorded groups, including the actual month/year labels, keyboard tabs, mobile menu and no-JavaScript content. Each produced a coherent fictional product page; the functional counts do not rank their visual quality.

The observed process adds context: the Fabius runs read the pinned design reference, and its second run measured a mobile overflow, changed the artwork container and retested. The baseline also planned, tested, revised presentation and checked keyboard behavior. More tool calls alone are not a benefit score.

The mobile captures reveal real tradeoffs. In the first pair, the Fabius page gives explanatory text more room but delays the product illustration; in the second pair, its long headline pushes the preview beyond the opening viewport, while the baseline shows more product. The next design check should examine what visitors actually see before scrolling.

Timing and output length change direction between repeats: the baseline is shorter/faster in the first pair, and Fabius is shorter/faster in the second. Two pairs on a shared environment do not establish a consistent speed or output-length effect.

review.implication: The app has a coherent identity and a readable grouping of workspace, summary, controls and tasks. The project list also gives context to the task cards.

review.observation: Task cards put date, compact status selector and edit/delete controls on a shared bottom row. This keeps multiple cards visible, but project labels, tags, dates, sidebar details and summary captions use small, fine text.
review.implication: The board uses space efficiently, while secondary information and small action icons demand closer reading than the bold task titles.

review.observation: The centered form separates task title and project from a two-column status/priority row, followed by due date and tags. Required markers and input guidance are visible, and the title field has a strong focus outline. Cancel and Create task are differentiated.
review.implication: The layout supports a straightforward entry sequence and makes the focused control clear. Static appearance does not prove complete focus trapping or assistive-technology behavior.

review.observation: Malformed JSON produces a prominent warm-tinted alert above the main heading, with an explicit failure title, a file-format explanation and a Dismiss button. The existing board remains visible below it.
review.implication: The error is hard to overlook and gives a recovery direction. The capture receipt confirms unchanged stored bytes for this input; the visible alert could also state that preservation explicitly.

review.observation: The active search shows one matching task and a Clear filters control, but empty status columns say Room for the next step and Completed work will land here. The summary still shows existing completed tasks outside the filter.
review.implication: Those empty-state messages sound like an empty board rather than excluded search results. Context-specific wording such as No matching tasks would make the filtering state clearer.

review.observation: The mobile view keeps a full-width New task button, three summary cards, search and filters within the opening screen; the top of the first status column reaches its lower edge. Primary content fits the width, but metadata, summary captions and filter text are small.
review.implication: The compact arrangement brings board navigation into view sooner, at the cost of finer text. A complete task card still requires scrolling, and this single capture does not evaluate the remainder of the mobile board.

review.observation: The desktop separates a persistent workspace rail from the board. The board title and dark New task button are prominent, followed by a summary, search/filter controls and three clearly named status columns.
review.implication: The major places and primary action are easy to identify, and the status columns provide a stable organizing structure.

review.observation: The top introduction, progress summary and spacious filters occupy a substantial band above the task cards. The left rail also devotes space to editorial copy and an illustration. Individual cards have generous padding and a full-width status select.
review.implication: The layout is calm and readable, but a working user scans relatively few complete cards in the first desktop viewport. Reducing introductory chrome or offering a denser board mode would improve task visibility.

review.observation: Serif page headings, bold sans-serif task titles, pale neutral/green surfaces and thin borders recur across the board and form. The restrained rust accent appears in progress, priority and visible focus treatment; priority also has a word and directional icon.
review.implication: The application presents a consistent identity and makes task titles more prominent than metadata without relying only on color for priority.

review.observation: The modal has distinct labels, required/optional markers, supporting constraints, grouped status/priority fields and clearly separated Cancel/Create actions. The currently focused title field has a conspicuous outline.
review.implication: The captured form tells users what each field expects and where the keyboard focus is. The screenshot does not establish complete keyboard or screen-reader conformance.

review.observation: The filtered board shows one matching card, an explicit matching count, a Clear filters control and readable empty states in the other columns. The malformed-import notice names invalid JSON and states that the existing board has not changed.
review.implication: The captured feedback explains both the current filtered view and the failed import. The capture receipt separately confirms unchanged stored bytes for this one malformed input; it is not a claim about all import cases.

review.observation: At the captured mobile first visit, the brand/header, large board title, introduction, New task button and expanded progress overview take nearly the entire viewport. Search appears near the bottom, and no task card is visible. The visible elements fit the width without obvious overlap.
review.implication: The mobile opening favors presentation over immediate access to existing work. Collapsing or shortening the introductory overview would bring the task board into view sooner.

review.observation: The desktop frame separates project navigation in a left rail, workspace actions in a top strip, an introductory heading, and three named task columns. A dark New task button is distinct from the quieter import and export controls.
review.implication: The visual hierarchy provides identifiable places for navigation, creation, and reviewing existing work.

review.observation: A large introductory area, a broad four-part overview, and a second Project board heading precede the search and task columns. Cards are generously spaced, with the next row only partly visible at the bottom of the desktop capture.
review.implication: The overview receives substantial emphasis, while fewer existing tasks are visible without scrolling.

review.observation: Cream and pale neutral surfaces, dark ink, restrained olive accents, and repeated fine borders form a consistent interface. The introductory heading mixes bold sans lettering with an italic serif phrase; task titles remain bold and visually separate from lighter project labels and tags.
review.implication: The expressive heading adds identity while the repeated task styling makes the board easier to scan. Fine secondary metadata still requires closer attention than the task titles.

review.observation: The centered form shows explicit title and project labels with Required markers, paired status and priority controls, an optional date field with a calendar affordance, and optional tags with comma and length guidance. The title field has a visible focus outline, and Save task is visually stronger than Cancel.
review.implication: Required input, optional input, and the completion action are understandable from the captured form; the screenshot alone does not establish complete keyboard or screen-reader operation.

review.observation: The filtered board displays the requested task, a matching count, Clear filters, and empty-column copy that explicitly says no tasks are in view. The malformed import capture shows a pale red notice stating: Import failed: This is not valid JSON. Your board is unchanged.
review.implication: The search copy distinguishes an empty filtered view from an empty workspace. The import notice explains both the invalid input and the intended preservation outcome; the capture receipt separately records unchanged stored bytes for this one malformed input.

review.observation: At 360 by 800, the brand strip, a wrapped Project board breadcrumb, introduction, New task action, and a two-by-two overview fill almost the entire first viewport. The Project board heading appears near the bottom; search controls and task cards are below the captured viewport. No overlapping or clipped primary text is visible.
review.implication: Task creation is available early, but reviewing or searching existing work requires scrolling past the overview. A more compact mobile introduction or overview would bring those actions into view sooner.

review.observation: The desktop separates workspace and project navigation in a left rail, an introductory heading and New task action, a summary strip, and a clearly labelled Studio board with search and three status columns. Card titles are visually stronger than project names, tags, and dates.
review.implication: Navigation, creation, overview, and individual work items have identifiable positions and a consistent reading order.

review.observation: A cream and sage palette, dark green text, serif display headings, repeated thin borders, and small line icons are consistent across the board and side rail. Project labels, date text, tags, and secondary explanatory lines are considerably smaller and lighter than task titles.
review.implication: The repeated visual treatment is coherent, and the title hierarchy supports scanning. Users must look more closely to read fine metadata or distinguish the small edit and delete icons; this is not a measured contrast or hit-area finding.

review.observation: The form gives title and project explicit required labels, marks due date and tags optional, explains tag limits, and shows a strong focus outline on the title. The date field displays YYYY-MM-DD as a plain text entry without a visible calendar affordance. Create task is visually stronger than Cancel.
review.implication: The required fields and save action are clear. Date entry depends on recognizing and typing the shown format, which is a usability tradeoff rather than evidence of invalid date handling.

review.observation: The requested Research task appears with its title, High priority badge, evidence and launch tags, and date. Searching its title leaves that single card in the In progress column, shows a matching count and Clear filters, and labels the other columns No matching tasks in this column.
review.implication: The task representation exposes the requested attributes. The search state explicitly distinguishes absent matches from a workspace with no tasks.

review.observation: The malformed import state shows a prominent warm notice headed Import could not be completed, followed by This file is not valid JSON. Your prior board has not been replaced. A Dismiss control is visible and existing task cards remain on screen.
review.implication: The notice explains the cause and preservation outcome in the same place. The capture receipt separately records unchanged stored bytes for this malformed input; the image alone does not establish complete import safety.

review.observation: At 360 by 800, the sidebar becomes a compact top identity strip, the heading fits on one line, and the summary arranges three counts above a progress row. New task, search, and all three filters appear in the first viewport. The first task-column heading begins near the bottom, while task cards are below the captured viewport. No overlapping or clipped primary text is visible.
review.implication: Creation and filtering are available before scrolling, but inspecting existing tasks still requires moving past the introduction and overview. A more compact overview could place actual work items closer to the initial viewport.

baseline.reviewMethod: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

lessons: In the first pair, the Fabius application meets all 16 primary groups and the baseline meets 15. In the second pair, both meet 15. The confirmed miss in three of four artifacts is specific: after a pointer-opened dialog closes with Escape, WebKit leaves focus on the page body. Opening the same dialog by keyboard passes. This is one observed advantage in one pair, not a consistent win across both repetitions.

All four applications meet the primary storage, import validation, recovery and stale-write groups across the recorded browser configurations. These are meaningful local-app scenarios, including hostile text and corrupt storage; they are not a security certification or a guarantee about untested workflows.

The retrospective trace review shows planning, testing and correction in both conditions. It also records gaps, such as the second baseline run having no recorded full main-suite rerun after its later source edits. The independent grader evaluated the final immutable artifact in every case.

An additional exploratory probe found that a project literally named all collides with the project-filter sentinel in the first baseline app and the second Fabius app. The other two apps distinguish the project correctly. Stored data remains intact. This probe was added after initial outcomes, applied to all four artifacts and kept outside the primary scores. A follow-up brief should distinguish filter identity from a user-entered project name.

The mobile captures show that overview panels often push actual tasks below the opening viewport. The next design check should assess access to tasks and filters, alongside readable forms, recovery messages and empty states.

Fabius finished faster and emitted fewer output tokens in both recorded application pairs. Extra instruction and retrieval costs remain part of the treatment, and native input usage is available in each receipt. Two repetitions on a shared environment do not establish a general speed or cost advantage.
